data.title: PM urges push up value chain
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul presided over the National Economic and Social Development Board's (NESDB) annual meeting to discuss the draft 2028–2032 NESDB plan.

data.title: Govt seeks aid against proxy firms
data.description: The Department of Business Development (DBD) has sent information on more than 100,000 companies with foreign directors or shareholders to 43 embassies, seeking cooperation in tackling nominee businesses.

data.title: Govt eyes new accommodation law
data.description: The government has proposed replacing the Hotel Act with a new law designed to bring more accommodation businesses into the regulatory system.

data.title: Disaster insurance cover rolls out nationwide today
data.description: The government is set to launch a nationwide disaster insurance programme covering about 30 million households from 12am today (Thursday), providing protection against floods, windstorms and earthquakes.

data.title: BMA says it's on top of Chao Phraya water levels
data.description: The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) has assured residents that Chao Phraya water levels remain manageable, as they are already falling in Klong Chan and other flooded areas.

data.title: PM sets up war room for flooding
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has ordered the Disaster Prevention and Mitigation Department to establish a daily flood war room to coordinate nationwide data and speed up emergency responses.

data.title: Court route urged over Senate poll
data.description: A legal forum on the controversial 2024 Senate selection has urged candidates who believe they were adversely affected by alleged systematic collusion to petition the Constitutional Court through the Ombudsman, arguing this could provide a route to challenge the legitimacy of the entire Senate selection process.

data.title: Blame game for floods steps up
data.description: The government failed to manage the flood crisis, issuing warnings too late and responding ineffectively, says People's Party (PP) leader Natthaphong Ruengpanyawut.

data.title: Only 18% of 10,000-bag backlog cleared at Suvarnabhumi
data.description: A total of 10,000 pieces of luggage piled up at Suvarnabhumi airport between Sept 26 and 28 as a result of flooding and operational failures by Thai Airways International, with only 18% cleared as of Wednesday, according to Transport Minister Phiphat Ratchakitprakarn.

data.title: PM defends handing out cash to flood victims
data.description: Sparking online debate after being captured on a Facebook live stream , Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul was seen handing out cash to flood-hit residents of communities in Sai Mai district of Bangkok late on Tuesday.

data.title: Pattaya prosecutors indict duo in Russian siblings’ deaths
data.description: PATTAYA - Pattaya prosecutors have indicted ex-convict Thana Kerdthong and his alleged accomplice on nine charges including murder in the deaths of two Russian siblings whose bodies were found buried in Bang Lamung district of Chon Buri in late July.

data.title: Nonthaburi raises red flags, reinforces flood barriers
data.description: Nonthaburi Municipality has raised red flags warning of critically high water levels and ordered sandbags to strengthen a 10-kilometre-long flood barrier along the Chao Phraya River following an increase in water discharge rates from the Chao Phraya dam in Chai Nat province.

data.title: Thai Airways suspends cargo intake amid flood disruption
data.description: Thai Airways International has announced a temporary suspension of inbound, outbound and transit cargo acceptance at its cargo terminal at Suvarnabhumi Airport from Oct 1-6 due to flooding disrupting staff travel and warehouse operations.

data.title: Tourist rafts, hundreds of fish cages hit Mae Klong dam
data.description: KANCHANABURI - A salvage operation was under way on Wednesday after strong currents on the storm-swollen Mae Klong river sent several tourist rafts and hundreds of fish cages smashing into the Mae Klong dam in Tha Muang district.

data.title: Storm-fed plankton bloom seen around Koh Lan
data.description: PATTAYA — The sea around Koh Lan, a popular island destination just off Pattaya in Chon Buri province, turned green on Wednesday, surprising some tourists unfamiliar with the phenomenon of a plankton bloom following heavy rainfall.

data.title: More rain forecast next week
data.description: More thundershowers are expected across Thailand between Sunday and Tuesday, with Bangkok and vicinity also warned of downpours, according to the Meterological Department.

data.title: Bangkok's oldest amusement park facing 6-month closure from flood damage
data.description: Bangkok's 118-acre Siam Amazing Park has announced a temporary six-month closure after nearly the entire complex suffered severe flood damage and has remained submerged for five days.

data.title: Floods across four regions, 40 fatalities
data.description: Ongoing floods have spread to cover about 2,700 square kilometres and have killed 40 people with the most affected areas being the Central Plains, government spokesman Ekkapob Pianpises said on Wednesday.

data.title: Thai Airways suspends cargo intake from Oct 1-6 amid flood disruption
data.description: Thai Airways International has announced a temporary suspension of inbound, outbound and transit cargo acceptance at its cargo terminal at Suvarnabhumi Airport from Oct 1-6 due to flooding disrupting staff travel and warehouse operations.

data.title: PM caught handing out cash to flood victims
data.description: Sparking online debate after being captured on a Facebook live stream , Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul was seen handing out cash to flood-hit residents of communities in Bangkok's Sai Mai district late on Tuesday.

data.title: Bangkok's City Hall reports flooding on about 10 roads
data.description: The Drainage and Sewerage Department of the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) reported flooding on about 10 roads in the capital on Wednesday morning, with water levels ranging from seven to 20 centimetres.

data.title: Bangkok opens shelter for animals rescued from floodwaters
data.description: Dogs and cats displaced by severe flooding in Bangkok can now receive temporary shelter, health assessments and medical care at the Prawet Animal Shelter, the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) announced on Wednesday.

data.title: Bangkok's City Hall reported flooding on about 10 roads
data.description: The Drainage and Sewerage Department of the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) reported flooding on about 10 roads in the capital on Wednesday morning, with water levels ranging from seven to 20 centimetres.

data.title: Seed rights split growers from farmers
data.description: Thailand is preparing to discuss adopting UPOV 1991 with the European Union as part of free trade negotiations next month, with the proposed rules drawing support from seed producers but opposition from farmer groups concerned about restrictions on seed saving and exchange.

data.title: 13 more Chao Phraya piers go under contract
data.description: The Marine Department is pressing ahead with a 200-million-baht programme to develop 29 smart piers along the Chao Phraya River in Bangkok and surrounding areas, with all due to be completed by June 2028.

data.title: 4 NHA condo projects get nod
data.description: The government on Tuesday approved four apartment projects by the National Housing Authority (NHA), offering more opportunities for low-income people to access high-quality housing at a reasonable price.

data.title: Cops nab 2 for arson attack
data.description: Police have arrested a Turkish man, 31, and his ex-girlfriend, 40, a former sales manager, over an arson attack on a company in Bang Khae district of the capital.

data.title: PP demands QR codes off list ballots
data.description: People's Party (PP) list MP Parit Wacharasindhu has called for barcodes to be removed from party-list election ballots after the Constitutional Court ruled that their use was constitutional but warned that such markings could undermine public confidence in the secrecy of voting.
